name: Veldtmann Pressline Assembly Line Full Kit
description:
A complete assembly line worker's kit issued by Veldtmann Industrial for pressline floor operations — stamping, forming, and quality inspection of fabricated metal components. The uniform jacket is a medium-weight royal blue synth-cotton blend with snap-front closure, elasticated cuffs that tighten against wrist augmentation ports to prevent snagging in machinery, and a Veldtmann Industrial chest emblem — a stylized press-stamp in yellow on a black field — embroidered at the left breast. The back panel carries the worker's station number in large yellow stencil print. The trousers match in royal blue, with articulated knees, two front slash pockets, and a sewn-in kneeling pad at the right knee — a small mercy for inspection posture on the concrete floor. A slim hi-vis yellow stripe runs down the outer leg seam on both sides.

A white hard hat with Veldtmann's press-stamp logo and an elastic sweatband is standard issue; this one has been personalized with a strip of family photos laminated under clear tape on the inside brim — visible only to the wearer. Safety glasses with side shields hang around the neck on a breakaway cord. Underfoot: Veldtmann Steelcap 7 boots in black with yellow toe-cap striping. Hearing protection — molded yellow foam plugs on a behind-the-neck band — sits ready around the collar. The outfit is clean at shift start: royal blue pressed, steel-toes wiped. By shift end, there's stamping oil on the cuffs and metal dust in every crease.
functionality: Machinery-safe elasticated wrist cuffs (aug-port compatible), articulated knees, sewn-in kneeling pad, hi-vis leg striping, hard hat with sweat band, breakaway safety glass cord, steel-toe boots, behind-neck hearing protection band
what_it_says: A Veldtmann assembly line worker — steady employment, mandatory safety compliance, the kind of job that comes with PPE audits and a floor supervisor who counts heads at shift start. The laminated family photos under the hard hat brim are invisible to management and essential to the worker: a private world maintained inside the institutional one. The pressed uniform at shift start signals someone who still believes in showing up right, even if the floor will wreck it by noon.
manufacturer: Veldtmann Industrial — fully corponation-issued uniform and PPE
price_range: Φ 150–Φ 200 (corponation-issued; dock replacement fees apply per item)
story_hooks: The station number stenciled on the back of a worker's jacket matches a station that was officially decommissioned after a fatal accident — but someone is still clocking into it each shift, and the output logs show full production.

The laminated photos under the hard hat brim include one face that a player character recognizes — someone who is supposed to be dead, standing in an outdoor market scene with a timestamp from eight months ago.

A Veldtmann floor worker has been quietly documenting safety violations in a hand-written log hidden inside the kneeling pad of their work trousers, and they need someone they can trust to get it out of the facility.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian assembly line uniform that reads as distinctly blue-collar and corporation-issued. The silhouette is functional and slightly boxy — designed for movement and machinery interaction rather than aesthetics. The wearer appears as a standardized unit of labor, marked by high-visibility yellow accents and official branding. There's a deliberate anonymity to it, broken only by personal touches like the helmet's hidden photo strip.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso and arms to allow machinery operation; articulated knees provide flexibility for crouching and inspection posture. Cuffs are elasticated and form-fitting around wrist augmentation ports — a practical detail that acknowledges the cyborg workforce. Trousers sit at natural waist with a slight taper at ankle to meet boots cleanly.
physical_description.primary_material: Medium-weight royal blue synth-cotton blend for the jacket and trousers — durable, easy to clean of industrial oils and metal particulates. Reinforced areas in ballistic-grade weave at stress points. Hard hat is injection-molded polymer. Boots are treated leather with steel-reinforced toe caps.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly stiff synthetic blend with a subtle matte finish that hides grease stains. Fabric has a slight nap from dust accumulation. Reinforced seams are visibly topstitched. The hard hat has a slightly grippy outer surface. Boots show scuff resistance with a minor sheen.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant royal blue throughout jacket and trousers; accent hi-vis yellow on leg stripes, toe-cap striping, foam ear plugs, and the stenciled station number. The chest emblem is yellow on black. White hard hat with yellow logo accent. Black boots with yellow details.
physical_description.closures: Snap-front closure on the jacket for quick donning/removal during shift changes. Trousers feature a traditional fly closure. Elasticated cuffs use friction-fit tension against augmentation ports. Breakaway cord on safety glasses for emergency quick-release. Hearing protection band sits behind neck.
distinctive_features: Veldtmann press-stamp logo embroidered in yellow on black at left breast
Large yellow stencil-printed station number on back panel
Elasticated cuffs designed to cinch around wrist augmentation ports without snagging
Sewn-in kneeling pad at right knee for inspection floor work
Yellow hi-vis stripe running down both outer leg seams
White hard hat with laminated family photos hidden under clear tape on inside brim — personal touch in standardized issue
Molded yellow foam hearing protection with behind-the-neck band
Safety glasses with side shields on breakaway cord
Steelcap 7 boots with yellow toe-cap striping
Visible wear pattern: stamping oil on cuffs, metal dust in seams by shift end
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class) — this is a corporation-issued uniform for manual factory labor. The quality is solid and functional, not cheap, but it explicitly marks the wearer as a floor worker, not management or skilled trade.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this says you are a Veldtmann pressline operator — a human component in a vast manufacturing pipeline. The hidden family photos suggest someone clinging to personal identity within a standardized, dehumanizing labor structure. The augmentation-port-aware cuff design acknowledges that cyborg workers are routine at this tier, though the presence of the photos implies the wearer is still human enough to want reminders of what that means.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and pressed at shift start; by end of shift, broken-in with visible oil stains on cuffs, metal dust embedded in fabric folds, and minor scuffs on boots. Hard hat may have small dents from minor bumps. The overall impression is 'clean enough to be regulation-compliant, worn enough to be real.'
